title: Father Sandro Jimenez visits Orlando to strengthen mission ties with Las Lomas region
text:
Father Sandro Jimenez visits Orlando to strengthen mission ties with Las Lomas region
Father Sandro Jimenez, the first priest officially assigned to the Las Lomas region of Orlando’s sister diocese in the Dominican Republic, visited the United States from Aug. 2-9 to connect with those supporting his community. His visit marked the first time a priest from Las Lomas traveled to meet with the Diocese of Orlando mission office and its supporters.
“Coming to the United States for the first time is a beautiful experience, but especially interesting because I wanted to see the place from where this love for Las Lomas comes,” Father Jimenez said.
During his stay, Father Jimenez met with mission directors, deacons, and local communities. He visited sites such as the Basilica of the National Shrine of Mary, Queen of the Universe and NASA. He also celebrated Mass and spoke at St. John Vianney Parish in Orlando. “I am not here as a tourist, but to bear witness of the love you all have for my community, for my mountains, for my people,” he told those gathered at St. John Vianney.
Father Jimenez reflected on the changes in Las Lomas over the past 30 years, saying, “When we say Las Lomas, we are talking about nine very poor communities. They lived in the mountains, they had no school, no potable water, no highways, no electricity. It is surprising to see how much has happened through the collaboration of the mission and its volunteers. Today our children have schools, water to drink, and our families have houses. Young people can go to university thanks to the mission. The mission is important because it brought health, education, homes, and spirituality, which is indispensable.”
The area now has two deacons as a result of ongoing evangelization efforts. Father Jimenez said of his parishioners, “They have no material wealth, but they have God in their hearts. I go to bring them the Gospel and I leave evangelized. I am so grateful to God for letting me be in the midst of these people. It is marvelous.”
Raquel Céspedes, director of Orlando’s mission office, said Father Jimenez’s visit was significant because “Never did a priest from Las Lomas cross paths to personally come to know the place from which so many efforts...for the Dominican people was born.” She added that his trip “adds a new page to that story: a page that reminds us that bridges of faith are built in both directions.”
The Diocese of Orlando was established in 1968 and includes 79 parishes across several counties; it is currently led by Bishop James Noonan and supports numerous missions throughout Central Florida and abroad, according to The Diocese of Orlando.
